ABSTRACT: An efficient electrochemical bromocyclization of
allenols has been realized for the synthesis of spirocyclic 2,5-
dihydrofurans. The reaction used commercially available and
nontoxic KBr as the brominating source in a simple setup under
open-air conditions. Notably, optically active products can be
obtained from optically active 2,3-allenols without any racemiza-
tion, further enhancing the synthetic utility.
S
pirocyclic frameworks are prevalent in natural products or
pesticides and frequently recognized as chiral scaffolds for
synthesizing chiral ligands.
1−3
Of particular interest are the
oxygen-containing spirocyclic compounds with their enhanced
three-dimensional structures, which are significant motifs in
various drugs and biologically active molecules, such as
hemostatic and filifolinol, due to their interactions with specific
protein receptors or enzymes (Scheme 1a).
4−6
Thus, the wide-
range importance of these compounds has driven the
advancement of new synthetic strategies to facilitate their
production.
7
In recent years, electrochemical anodic oxidations have
emerged as mild, efficient, and environmentally friendly
strategies for the synthesis of complex molecules.
8
Notably,
the electrochemical halogenation of alkenes or alkynes using
commercially available, nontoxic, and atom-efficient MX/HX
systems has been developed to avoid the use of hazardous or
expensive halogenation reagents (such as dihalogen or N-
halogensuccinimide), transition metal salts (e.g., CuX
2
, FeX
3
,
etc.), and stoichiometric strong oxidants.
9−12
Based on our previous reports on the easy synthesis of
tertiary allenols,
13
we investigated whether the electrochemical
halocyclization of allenols
14,15
could serve as an efficient and
convenient method for accessing oxygen-containing spirocyclic
products C. However, two challenges remained (Scheme 1b):
first, engaging different double bonds with similar properties in
allenes could yield spirocyclic products A;
16
second, ring-
expansion reactions could produce nonspirocyclic products
B.
12a
Herein, we describe our efforts to develop the
electrochemical bromocyclization of allenols for the synthesis
of spirodihydrofuran with a useful C−Br bond handle for
downstream functionalizations as a starting point (Scheme 1c).
To assess the feasibility of this strategy, we commenced our
study by reacting allenol 1a with KBr. Gratifyingly, the
spirocyclic product 2a was obtained in 87% yield using a
graphite plate as the anode and a platinum plate as the
cathode, with CH

examination showed that the yield of 2a decreased with either
a lower or higher current (Table 1, entries 9−12). Scaling up
the reaction to 1.0 mmol resulted in a moderate yield of 76%
(Table 1, entry 13). Through further efforts, we found that
increasing the reaction concentration, decreasing the reaction
time could enhance the production of 2a, which was isolated in
84% yield on the 1.0 mmol scale (Table 1, entry 14).
With the optimized reaction conditions established, we
explored the substrate scope of this electrochemical
bromocyclization protocol of allenols (Scheme 2). As a
comparison, the reaction of 1a with KCl and KI under the
standard conditions afforded 3-chloro- and 3-iodo-dihydrofur-
an products 3a and 4a in 35% and 9% yields, respectively. A
wide range of tertiary 2,3-allenols underwent bromocyclization
smoothly, yielding 2,5-dihydrofuran derivatives 2 in good to
excellent yields. First, we evaluated the ring sizes of cyclic
tertiary 2,3-allenols. Various substrates with carbocycles of
different sizes proved viable in our electrochemical trans-
formation, generating a range of spirocyclic products in yields
of 60−84%. Notably, highly strained four-membered allenol 1b
and medium-sized 12-membered allenol 1e served as suitable
substrates, affording products 2b and 2e in 60% and 75%
yields, respectively. An acetal moiety may also survive, yielding
76% of 2f. Moreover, substrates containing heterocycles
performed well, providing the corresponding oxa- or aza-
spirocyclic products 2g and 2h in yields of 74% and 81%,
respectively. A variety of synthetically useful groups, including
cyclopropyl (2i), phenyl (2j), halide (2k), and allyl (2l) groups
were well-tolerated. Beyond cyclic tertiary allenols, this
electrochemical strategy may also be extended to acyclic
tertiary allenols [dimethyl (1m), diallyl (1n), and dibenzyl
(1o)]. Remarkably, a trisubstituted allenol enabled access to a
4-bromide-substituted spirocyclic 2,5-dihydrofuran product 2p
in 57% yield. The protocol also proved effective for primary
allenol 1q, where both R
3
and R
4
are n-propyl. Finally,
bispirocyclic product 2r was smoothly synthesized.
Furthermore, when optically active allenols (R)-1h and (S)-
1h were subjected to the electrochemical bromocyclization
protocol under the standard conditions, the corresponding
chiral spirocyclic products (S)-2h and (R)-2h were obtained
efficiently without any loss of ee. A single-crystal X-ray
diffraction analysis was conducted to determine the absolute
configuration of (R)-2h (Scheme 3).
The reaction was successfully scaled up to a 4.0 mmol scale
using a simple and readily made device (see Figure S3 in the
Supporting Information), yielding product 2g in 73% yield
(Scheme 4a). The synthetic utility of the spirocyclic products
is demonstrated (Scheme 4b): Product 2g was readily reduced
by p-toluenesulfonyl hydrazide at 135 °C to afford spiro-
tetrahydrofuranyl bromide 5 in a highly stereoselective
manner.
17
By comparison, when 2g was subjected to 0.6
equiv of NiCl
2

4

tetrahydrofuran 6 was obtained in 81% yield.

Control experiments showed that when substrate 1a was
reacted with molecular Br
2

obtained, but with significantly reduced yields of 28% and 25%,
respectively (Scheme 5, entries 2 and 3), indicating the
advantage of the electrosynthesis. Interestingly, the addition of
KBr increased the yield of 2a to 47% (Scheme 5, entry 4). We
reasoned that the slow releasing of the Br
2
is responsible for
the higher yield observed in the current study.
A plausible reaction mechanism is proposed in Scheme 6. At
the anode, a bromide anion is oxidized to a bromine radical,
subsequently combining to form molecular Br
2
, which would
interact with Br
−
to produce Br
3
−
. This Br
2
electrophilically
interacted with (R)-1h to generate the bromonium ion
intermediate int. I. Intramolecular anti-nucleophilic attack by
the hydroxy group from the opposite side followed by
deprotonation, yielded the final product (R)-2h. Concurrently,
at the cathode, water is continuously reduced to generate OH
−
and gaseous H
2
.
In summary, we have described a highly efficient electro-
chemical synthetic method for spirocyclic 2,5-dihydrofuran
derivatives from allenols. This approach operates under metal
catalyst-free and exogenous oxidant-free conditions, utilizing
commercially available and nontoxic KBr as the brominating
source. The method enjoys ease of handling and mild reaction
conditions preventing racemization with the optically active
substrates. Further studies in this area including control of the
cyclization mode are currently ongoing in our laboratory.

ABSTRACT: An eficient electrochemical bromocyclization of
allenols has been realized for the synthesis of spirocyclic 2,5-
dihydrofurans. The reaction used commercially available and
nontoxic KBr as the brominating source in a simple setup under
open-air conditions. Notably, optically active products can be
obtained from optically active 2,3-allenols without any racemiza-
tion, further enhancing the synthetic utility.

In summary, we have described a highly eficient electro-
chemical synthetic method for spirocyclic 2,5-dihydrofuran
derivatives from allenols. This approach operates under metal
catalyst-free and exogenous oxidant-free conditions, utilizing
commercially available and nontoxic KBr as the brominating
source. The method enjoys ease of handling and mild reaction
conditions preventing racemization with the optically active
substrates. Further studies in this area including control of the
cyclization mode are currently ongoing in our laboratory.
